note: The Centres of Excellence are the most physically distributed thing in the whole relationship. They sit in district agricultural stations, not in capitals, and they are where an abstraction about cooperation turns into a particular crop in a particular place. The list below is as published by the Embassy of Israel in New Delhi. Counts of how many exist differ between sources and dates, and those differences are shown rather than resolved.

counts.text: 37 approved, 29 fully operational across 12 states, 8 at various stages
43 approved, 35 operational, sixth work plan 2024 to 2026
35 operating, 8 being jointly operationalised, more than a million farmers trained

Dapoli in Ratnagiri for mango, Nagpur for citrus, Rahuri for pomegranate, Aurangabad for mango

Dharwad for vegetables, Bagalkot for pomegranate, Kolar for mango
Hoshiarpur for fruits, Kartarpur for vegetables, Bhatinda for brackish water
Kota for citrus, Bassi for pomegranate, Jaisalmer for date palm
Thally in Krishnagiri for floriculture, Reddiyarchathram in Dindigul for vegetables

villages: The Villages of Excellence programme extends the model outward from the centres. In 2021 it targeted eight states, with 13 Centres of Excellence covering 75 villages, on three pillars: modern agriculture infrastructure, capacity building and market linkage. The Embassy of India in Tel Aviv records 190 villages identified across 22 Centres of Excellence in 12 states.

water.text: On 24 October 2018 Punjab signed a memorandum with Israel's Mekorot, under which Mekorot would prepare a water conservation and management plan for the state.
On 14 June 2022 Israel and Haryana signed a joint declaration on integrated water resources management and capacity building.
On 10 December 2024, at the Rising Rajasthan summit in Jaipur, the Israeli Foreign Ministry and Rajasthan's Water Resources Department signed a joint declaration on water cooperation.
Aqwise, in a joint venture with Triveni Engineering, operates a plant with a capacity of 160,000 cubic metres a day supplying drinking water to Agra.
Tahal Group built a water supply system for 131 villages, at a stated value of USD 74 million.
Ayala took a 2017 contract for an eight kilometre stretch of the Yamuna.
Metzerplas of the Metzer Group has manufactured drip irrigation equipment there since 2019.
Centres of water technology were agreed at IIT Madras and IIT Roorkee in May 2023.
